For stride-one causal convolutions, maximum receptive-field span is R = 1 + Σₗ(kₗ−1)dₗ; count every convolution, including both inside residual blocks. The original [NextItNet implementation](https://github.com/fajieyuan/WSDM2019-nextitnet/blob/master/ops.py) includes a two-convolution block with dilations d and 2d, adding 3d(k−1), and a bottleneck variant with one dilated convolution, adding d(k−1). Repeating dilation schedules continues accumulating context; resetting dilation does not reset historical reach. Residual connections preserve existing dependencies. Span can contain unreachable offsets when dilation schedules leave gaps.

Architectural inference: gating short- and long-dilation branches operating on contextualized hidden states cannot guarantee removal of older history. Even a pointwise branch inherits its input’s historical dependencies; gates and residual bypasses can also transmit them. Such gating controls transformations, not a strict history cutoff. A strictly bounded branch must start from raw embeddings restricted to the intended window, or upstream features with a proven dependency bound. For each output t, process only its permitted window; keep every branch input, gate and bypass within that bound. Verify by perturbing older inputs while holding the permitted window fixed and checking output invariance.

For reproducible causality, NextItNet explicitly left-pads by (k−1)d, uses VALID convolution, and normalizes channels separately at each timestep. In PyTorch, use [LayerNorm(C)](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.modules.normalization.LayerNorm.html) on B×L×C; training [BatchNorm1d](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.batchnorm.BatchNorm1d.html) aggregates over time and can leak future information. Implementation consequence: zero padding embeddings and reapply validity masks after biased convolutions, affine normalization and residual blocks, before subsequent temporal mixing. Mask padded losses. With left-padded histories, read the final nonpadding position—normally index L−1—not count−1.
